name: Patrick Lee
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2019); Hurun China (2021)
forbes_bio: Paper magnate Patrick Lee was born in Hainan, came to Hong Kong as an orphan and learned the art of trading from an uncle.
After early success in handbags Lee noticed that he was having trouble finding boxes for his exports, leading him to start a paper company.
Today, Lee & Man Paper is an industrial-packaging behemoth in China. Sons Raymond and Edmond run operations.
Lee also ventured into chemical production and set up Lee & Man Chemical in 2006, now headed by another son Norman.
forbes_facts: The Lee family is a big fan of horse racing. Their racehorses are all named after Bao Zhuang, or the Chinese term for packaging.

name: Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner
name_chinese: 伊娃·玛丽亚·布赫·海夫纳
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner's fortune mostly stems from her former stake in IT management software maker CA Technologies, acquired by Broadcom in 2020.
She inherited half of her father Walter's stake in the business when he died in June 2012, then the world's oldest billionaire at 101.
She and her brother, Martin Haefner, also inherited equal stakes in car dealer AMAG.
Bucher-Haefner sold her stake in AMAG to Martin, who is also a billionaire, in late 2018.
She runs Moyglare, a 500-acre horse farm in Ireland that was purchased by her father in 1962, home to around 100 horses today.

name: Wang Yanqing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Yanqing is the founder, chairman and CEO of Wuxi Lead Intelligent Equipment, one of the world's leading makers of equipment for the battery and electronics industries.
Lead counts Tesla, BMW, Panasonic, Samsung, CATL and BYD among its clients.
His son, Wang Lei, sits on the board.
The Shenzhen-listed company filed for a Hong Kong IPO in August 2025.

name: Martin Hetzner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Martin Hetzner is CEO of Hetzner, a German technology company he founded in 1997.
He is the sole owner of the business, which offers data-center management and IT services in Germany.
Hetzner had sales of more than 500 million euros in 2023, its most recent financial disclosures.
Hetzner is private and avoids public appearances.

name: Arvind Poddar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025)
forbes_bio: Arvind Poddar and his family control Balkrishna Industries, which provides off-highway tires for the agriculture, mining and construction sectors.
Poddar is chairman and managing director of the company while his son Rajiv is the joint managing director.
With roots in the textile business going back to 1951, Balkrishna Industries started making bicycle tires in 1963.
Poddar entered the off-highway tire market in the mid-1990s and now supplies to clients in Europe and the Americas.
In 2021, the company opened its newest factory in the western state of Maharashtra to manufacture agricultural and industrial tires.

name: Lindsay Fox
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Lindsay Fox owns Linfox, Australia's biggest private logistics company, with more than 5,000 trucks, including electric vehicles, across 12 countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
The company also owns a large industrial property portfolio, a half-share in a business park, two airports and currency-management outfit Armaguard.
Fox is no longer involved in day-to-day operations, leaving management to his son Peter, who is executive chairman and runs the logistics business.
His other sons Andrew and David run the property division and look after the airports respectively.
In January 2025, Linfox International Group acquired Singapore-based logistics company Masindo Logistic for an undisclosed amount to strengthen its foothold across the Asia-Pacific region.
forbes_facts: Fox also owns historic Melbourne amusement park Luna Park, more than 100 vintage cars on display for the public, a race track and four homes.
Fox quit his school for academically gifted boys at age 16 to become a truck driver like his father. He bought his first truck at 19.

name: Louise Lindh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Louise Lindh and her sister Katarina Martinson each own a 15% stake in their family's investment outfit, L.E. Lundbergforetagen AB.
The company has investments in property management and a variety of other businesses, including stakes in firms like truck-maker Volvo and Ericsson.
Both sisters have board seats in the group companies along with their father Fredrik Lundberg.
The company was founded by their grandfather Lars in 1944 as a construction outfit. Fredrik took over management of the firm in 1981.
Lindh runs the group's real estate outfit, and sits on the boards of paper company Holmen.
forbes_facts: In 2018, Lindh and her husband bought battery maker IAB? Global Holding for 36 million Swedish kronor, roughly $4 million.
Louise spent most of her childhood in Switzerland where the family had moved to avoid punitive taxes.

name: Mi Enhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2025); Hurun China (2001-2026)
forbes_bio: Mi is president of China's Xiangjiang Hualing Industry and Trade Group; he has led its expansion from a wholesale market into a conglomerate spanning trade, construction and logistics.
Mi Enhua founded Hualing in 1988.
Mi attended the inauguration of Philippines President Rodrigo Duterte in June 2016.

name: Steven Schonfeld
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010)
forbes_bio: Schonfeld is the founder of Schonfeld Strategic Advisors, a hedge fund with $17.5 billion in assets under management.
He first launched his business in 1988 as a proprietary trading firm specializing in short-term trading and converted it into a family office around 2009.
Schonfeld evolved into a multi-strategy hedge fund that opened to outside investors in 2016. Its flagship fund has never had a losing year.
He built a private nine-hole golf course on 44 acres in the backyard of his Old Westbury, New York home.

name: Matthew Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Matthew Pritzker and his sister Liesel Pritzker Simmons sued their family for a chunk of its Hyatt Hotels fortune and received around $500 million apiece in 2005.
Their uncle Jay Pritzker (d. 1999) founded the hotel chain and their uncle Donald Pritzker (d. 1972) managed and developed it.
Their father Robert Pritzker (d. 2011) ran the family's industrial conglomerate Marmon Group, which was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in a series of transactions beginning in 2008.
Three of Matthew and Liesel's step-siblings, seven cousins and their father's cousin Nick Pritzker are also billionaires.
Matthew invests his fortune through the Chicago-based Matthew Pritzker Company.

name: Anthony Casalena
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Anthony Casalena founded website building startup Squarespace in his University of Maryland dorm room in 2003.
Casalena founded Squarespace with a $30,000 loan from his parents.
Squarespace sells monthly or annual plans that range from a simple domain name and website to more advanced options for e-commerce.
He took Squarespace public in 2021, then took it private in October 2024 alongside UK private equity firm Permira.
Casalena owns more than 20% of Squarespace and remains CEO.

name: Joseph Bae
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2023-2025)
forbes_bio: Joseph Bae is co-CEO of storied private equity giant KKR, which has about $638 billion in assets under management.
He was appointed to the top job alongside Scott Nuttall after KKR cofounders Henry Kravis and George Roberts stepped down in October 2021.
Bae started his career at Goldman Sachs and joined KKR in 1996.
He led KKR's expansion into Asia and served on all its private market investment committees.
He cofounded The Asian American Foundation to build safety and inclusivity among AAPIs.
forbes_facts: Bae and his co-CEO Scott Nuttall began as KKR analysts together when they were 24.

name: Rosanna Armani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Rosanna Armani is the sister of billionaire fashion designer Giorgio Armani (d. September 2025).
She is a board member of Armani's namesake fashion firm but doesn't appear to have an executive role at the company.
Under the terms of Armani's will, Rosanna is entitled to 17% of the net proceeds from the sale or public listing of 45% of the company within five years of Armani's death.
She also inherited some of Armani's shares in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica as well as a stake in Armani's superyacht and his empire of luxury homes.
